name: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos (Tocco)
wikipedia: County Palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Naples
predecessors.text: Cephalonia, Zakynthos and possibly Ithaca: 'In 1357, Robert of Taranto ceded Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca to the governor of Corfu, Leonardo I Tocco'

successors.name: Despotate of Epirus
successors.text: the Tocco islands (Cephalonia, Zakynthos, Ithaca, Lefkada) with Angelokastron, joined to Ioannina under Carlo I Tocco: 'The Tocco ... were successful in gaining control over the Despotate of Epirus…

capitals.name: Castle of Saint George (Kastro Agiou Georgiou), near Peratata, Cephalonia

rulers.name: Leonardo I Tocco
rulers.title: Count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos

rulers.name: Carlo I Tocco
rulers.title: Count palatine of Cephalonia and Zakynthos, duke of Leukas

ledger.x: 1357: Robert of Taranto makes Leonardo I Tocco count palatine of Cephalonia, Zakynthos and Ithaca.

ca. 1362: Leonardo I gains Lefkada and the port of Vonitsa. Page: 'Probably by ca. 1362, and certainly before 1373, Leonardo also succeeded in gaining control over Lefkada and the port of Vonitsa'; the page names no grantor or previous holder. Vonitsa is not drawn.
ledger.cp: previous holders of Lefkada and Vonitsa (page silent)

ledger.x: 1408: Leonardo and Carlo Tocco take Glarentza from the Principality of Achaea.
February 1411: Carlo I Tocco is invited to Ioannina and unites it with the islands.
1411: the Tocco county is absorbed into Carlo I's Despotate of Epirus.

wars.name: Tocco-Spata wars
wars.outcome: Carlo I's siege of Angelokastron (1402-03) was repulsed and his 1406 raid on Acarnania and Arta failed to take the city, but Angelokastron fell to him within a year of Pal Shpata's 1406 cession to the Ottomans; the Albanians beat the Tocco army at Kranea in…

certainty.note: The island coasts are fixed by the sea, but who held Lefkada, Vonitsa and the mainland fortresses at which date rests on pages that say 'ca.
